correctness.rationale: In reciprocal state, flight and pulsing compose to an affine return of positive intercept and slope exp(-AT)/Q. Slope below one gives the unique attracting positive orbit; slope at least one sends the reciprocal state to infinity. The positive periodic orbit lies below A, so peaks are pre-pulse limits. Log integration gives the invariant integral and the scalar Floquet factor. Multiplying flight identities cancels cyclic state ratios; each resulting log term is strictly increasing from zero, so equality in the minimax bound forces all peaks equal. The resulting positive recovery times sum to T and determine the labeled gaps. Moving a pulse earlier across positive flight strictly increases the pre-pulse return map; comparison to the clustered fixed point is strict for m>1, with the clustered endpoint achieved only as a limit. Continuity (also at the clustered limit via the affine map) and connectedness give the full range; m=1 is the coincident-endpoint case. An independent exact reciprocal-map computation recovered 2/3, 16/21 and 9/8 in the stated example (/workspace/branches/audit_witnesses.py); the general result is analytical. The Floquet result is for fixed proportional factors, not fixed physical doses; it allows different peaks, not an injectivity claim about schedules.

value.rationale: The timing problem is meaningful precisely because the standard invasion scalar is blind to the prescribed gaps. The exact range and equality pattern tell how much worst susceptible exposure can vary and select the unique minimax schedule for any fixed heterogeneous strengths, not just one numerical optimizer. This is a result about susceptible exposure inside the stated model, not about actual infection burden or vaccination cost.
